problem: Prior zero-shot visual object navigation methods either need task-specific training for exploration or must rebuild/remap semantic value maps when the target changes, which is inefficient for single- and multi-object navigation.
motivation: Open-world navigation needs agents that can find arbitrary targets without retraining and can switch targets online. Frontiers are natural spatial anchors, so storing VLM semantic embeddings on frontiers should let new targets be scored by similarity without remapping.
key_idea: Build and maintain a training-free Frontier Embedding Graph whose nodes are frontiers holding VLM-derived, text-aligned semantic embeddings, updated by aggregating spatio-temporal relations across frontiers and scored by similarity to any new target.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract implies that decoupling stored frontier embeddings from a specific target text enables target switching without remapping, which benefits multi-object navigation.
method: Frontier Embedding Graph: nodes are frontiers holding spatially anchored semantic embeddings.
VLM-based initialization: visual observations are encoded into frontier embeddings via cross-modal alignment with target text descriptors.
Graph update: embeddings are aggregated across frontiers using spatio-temporal semantic relations.
Similarity scoring: frontiers are scored against a new target's text embedding online, without remapping, to pick the next exploration goal.
